headline_marked: [[Tawhid Hridoy smashes 350* to break Tamim Iqbal's first-class record]] in South Africa
headline: Tawhid Hridoy smashes 350* to break Tamim Iqbal's first-class record in South Africa
summary: Hridoy's unbeaten 350 against South Africa 'A' is now the highest individual score by a Bangladeshi in first-class cricket, surpassing Tamim's 334*.
details: Tawhid Hridoy has etched his name in history, becoming the first Bangladeshi batsman to score a triple century abroad and now holding the highest individual score in first-class cricket for Bangladesh. He remained unbeaten on 350 runs against South Africa 'A' in Potchefstroom.

This monumental innings surpasses the previous record of 334 not out, held by veteran opener Tamim Iqbal. Tamim achieved his record in 2019 during the Bangladesh Cricket League (BCL) playing for East Zone against Central Zone at Mirpur Sher-e-Bangla Stadium.

Hridoy's incredible feat came on the fourth and final day of the match. Bangladesh 'A' faced a collapse, losing two quick wickets early in the day, leaving Hridoy at 225 runs with only four wickets remaining.
He then forged a resilient partnership with number nine batsman Rejaur Rahman. Hridoy anchored one end with unwavering batting, accelerating his score to overtake Tamim's record.

Rejaur Rahman provided crucial support, remaining unbeaten on 31 runs off 110 balls in a significant ninth-wicket stand. Bangladesh 'A' declared their innings at 676 for 8, with Hridoy's name shining brightly with an unbeaten 350 off 481 balls.

headline: Homeopathic practitioner hacked to death in Natore; motive remains unclear
summary: A 60-year-old homeopathic practitioner was brutally attacked and killed in his chamber in Natore Sadar upazila. Police are investigating the incident, but the motive behind the killing is currently unknown.
details: A 60-year-old homeopathic practitioner, Md Anwarul Islam, was hacked to death in his chamber at Chandpur Market in Natore Sadar upazila on Wednesday night. The incident occurred around 7:30 PM while he was working, according to police.
Anwarul Islam, originally from Puthia upazila in Rajshahi, had been operating his chamber at Chandpur Bazar for several decades. He was known to keep his shop open until 9:00 PM daily.

Police recovered the body and sent it to Natore Sadar Hospital for autopsy. Officer-in-Charge Md Monsur Ahmed stated that no witnesses saw the attack, and authorities are actively investigating to identify the culprits.

Despite his long-standing presence in the area for over three decades, locals reported being unaware of any personal enmity or clear motive that could have led to his murder. The investigation continues to uncover the circumstances surrounding the tragic event.
caption:

Police recovered the body and sent it to Natore Sadar Hospital for autopsy. Officer-in-Charge Md Monsur Ahmed stated that no witnesses saw the attack, and authorities are actively investigating to identify the culprits.
